no-priors.name: No Priors
no-priors.bio: Podcast: Tokenization, Agentic Trading, Harmonic: Robinhood's Mission to Expand Ownership with CEO Vlad Tenev

html_en:
The gap between AI-augmented and non-augmented workers isn't closing — it's widening. That uncomfortable truth runs through today's feed like a live wire, touching everything from coding productivity to financial democracy to the geopolitics of data centers.

The Productivity Chasm Nobody Expected

Aaron Levie put into words what a lot of builders are quietly experiencing but hesitant to say out loud:

"We're starting to see plenty of examples of productivity gains that are an order of magnitude or two above output levels pre-AI. What's crazy is this gap doesn't appear to be diminishing over time. You'd think that we'd see a convergence in the lines because of AI, but it turns out the more depth you had before — and willingness now to take a different approach — gives you crazy leverage." — @levie

This is a striking inversion of the usual democratization narrative. The conventional wisdom held that AI would be a great equalizer — lifting all boats. Instead, Levie is describing a world where existing expertise compounds with AI rather than being substituted by it. The conditions he lists are specific: a right harness, domain depth, a relatively fresh codebase, fluency with multi-agent workflows, and low-friction deployment. Miss one and the multiplier shrinks considerably.

Andrej Karpathy provided an almost comically clean illustration of the same point. He took a curated YouTube channel list published by a friend, turned it into a fully functional streaming site — 47,000 "super nerdy" videos with a TV mode — and did it in three minutes via Claude Code. The product is called TristanTube. The implication is obvious: what would have taken a small team a week of work is now a Saturday afternoon impulse project for someone who knows what they're doing.

Claude's Pricing Ladder Gets Clearer

There's been real confusion in the market about Anthropic's Pro tier structure, and @thsottiaux stepped in to clarify:

"All Pro plans have no 5-hour limits, and give the following usage compared to Plus: Pro 100 = 10X, Pro 200 = 20X, Pro 500 = 50X, access to ultrafast." — @thsottiaux

He also floated a question that immediately picked up traction — would a Pro 50 tier make sense? — drawing over 1,300 likes, suggesting there's real appetite for a mid-range option between Plus and the current entry-level Pro. The tiering conversation reflects a broader maturation: the market is learning to price AI consumption the way it once learned to price cloud compute.

AI Agents Meet Financial Markets — Robinhood's Surprising Bet

The No Priors podcast this week features a genuinely surprising conversation with Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev, who has quietly built the company into something far stranger and more ambitious than the meme-stock app of public imagination.

Watch/Listen: No Priors — Tokenization, Agentic Trading, Harmonic: Robinhood's Mission to Expand Ownership with CEO Vlad Tenev

The headline number: agentic trading already has genuine product-market fit.

"AgenTik trading, clearly product market fit. We're seeing really strong adoption — over 150,000 customers have opened agentic trading accounts with us." — Vlad Tenev, No Priors

The broader thesis Tenev is building toward is one of radical democratization: institutional-grade tools — algorithmic trading, private market access, tokenized global assets — made available to anyone with a phone. His personal origin story sharpens the mission. He grew up in Bulgaria during the hyperinflation of the early 1990s, watching his grandfather convert his salary immediately into copper cookware to preserve value against a currency losing 2,000% annually. It's not an abstract commitment to financial inclusion — it's visceral.

"A society without broad ownership is inherently very unstable. It's a fragile society. And if you have more people that own things, they're more bought in, they have more stake in the outcome, and they become kind of defenders and protectors of the system." — Vlad Tenev

He also runs Harmonic, an effort to build a math superintelligence — and his critique of the current AI landscape sounds almost like a reformer's complaint: "It's too centralized. It's like AI companies with their big data centers and their employees using secret models to sort of do all this work." Coming from someone running a fintech giant with 120-country reach, that's a pointed observation about who actually benefits from the current AI moment.

The Geopolitics of Inference

Levie had a second, underappreciated thread worth flagging — a sharp piece of reasoning about where AI infrastructure actually needs to be located:

"Long running agents are now going to be the norm, which means it's ok to send off work to an AI factory somewhere and that work can essentially be largely done within that remote data center and a final result spit back to the user... Because the economic value of the task is so high relative to the latency sensitivity, you don't have to have the inference be particularly close to the user." — @levie

This reframes the data center siting debate considerably. Unlike streaming video or e-commerce, where milliseconds matter to user experience, agentic AI tasks — think: "research this vendor, draft a contract, flag the risks" — can tolerate round-trip latency measured in seconds or minutes. That changes the economics and the politics of where you build. Amjad Masad's observation that Kazakhstan's government is enthusiastically "AI-pilled" fits neatly here — countries that move early to host this infrastructure stand to gain enormously.

@adityaag put the investment corollary bluntly: if permitting and regulatory friction slows new datacenter construction, the existing hyperscalers win by default. The spice, as he puts it, must flow — and those who already hold capacity will extract the premium.

Odds and Ends: Stickers, Satire, and Startup Fate

Shawn Wang (@swyx) teased some impressive conference swag ahead of what sounds like a significant event next week. No spoilers, but the sticker game appears to be escalating industry-wide.

@nikunj published a sharply satirical thread on the anatomy of a Series A fundraise in 2025 — vague revenue graphs, manufactured FOMO, and the magic incantation of "long horizon agent swarms abilterared world models physical AI" — that lands because every line is, as he admits, individually true. Worth a full read if you've spent any time near a pitch deck recently.

And @zarazhangrui offered a quiet corrective to the fatalism that sometimes pervades startup discourse: "Startups' fates are MADE, not predetermined. Given one idea, there are 1000 ways to execute it." In a week full of talk about compounding advantages and structural winners, it's a useful reminder that the map is not the territory.
html_zh:
当AI重塑生产力的边界，金融民主化与代码自动化在同一周交汇——今天的科技圈，每个人都在用不同方式回答同一个问题：谁将拥有未来？

⚡ 三分钟搭建一个网站：Claude Code的「一次完成」时刻

Andrej Karpathy 本周展示了一个令人印象深刻的小实验：他看到朋友 Tristan 发布了一份优质 YouTube 频道推荐清单，于是用 Claude Code 用时三分钟、一次提示，直接构建出了一个名为 TristanTube 的完整网站——收录了 47,000 个极客向视频，还配备了"电视模式"供人懒散地躺着刷。

"47K 超极客向视频 + 电视模式随机播放。用 Claude Code 一次完成，耗时三分钟。"
—— @karpathy

这个细节的价值不在于网站本身，而在于它所指向的趋势：编程的"单次对话成本"正在快速趋近于零。这与 Box CEO Aaron Levie 本周的观察形成了呼应。

"我们开始看到大量生产力提升案例，其输出水平比 AI 出现前高出一到两个数量级……奇怪的是，这个差距并没有随时间缩小。你会以为 AI 会让所有人趋于平均，但事实是，你之前积累的越深，加上现在愿意换一种方式工作，给你带来的杠杆就越疯狂。"
—— @levie

Levie 补充说，这种效应目前在软件工程领域最为明显，但他预计很快会蔓延至科学研究、建筑工程、金融和网络安全等领域。

🏦 Robinhood 的野心：让 AI 替每个人交易

本周最值得细听的播客来自 No Priors，主角是 Robinhood 创始人兼 CEO Vlad Tenev。他描绘的不是一家股票交易 App，而是一个以"所有权"为核心使命的全球金融集团。

Watch/Listen: No Priors — Tokenization, Agentic Trading, Harmonic: Robinhood's Mission to Expand Ownership

"代理交易（Agentic Trading）显然已经找到了产品市场契合点。我们看到了非常强劲的采用率——超过 15 万名客户已经在我们这里开设了代理交易账户。"
—— Vlad Tenev

Tenev 成长于 1990 年代保加利亚的恶性通货膨胀环境，他的祖父用铜制厨具来保值财富——这段经历塑造了他对金融体系脆弱性的深刻理解。如今他把 Robinhood 定义为"所有权公司"：从零岁即可开设的 Trump 账户，到私募股权投资，再到代币化资产，目标是让全球 120 个国家的人都能接入资本市场。

"一个缺乏广泛所有权的社会，本质上是非常不稳定的……如果更多人拥有东西，他们就更有参与感，更有切身利益，他们就会成为这个体系的捍卫者。"
—— Vlad Tenev

值得关注的是他同步在推进的另一个项目：Harmonic，一个致力于构建数学超级智能的计划。他对当前 AI 生态的批评也颇为犀利：

"现在太中心化了——AI 公司用他们的大型数据中心和员工，使用秘密模型来完成所有工作。"
—— Vlad Tenev

🌐 AI 工厂的地缘政治：算力在哪里，权力就在哪里

Levie 本周还贡献了另一篇值得深思的分析，主题是 AI 推理的地理属性——或者说，它为何可以几乎没有地理属性。

"长时运行的 Agent 将成为常态，这意味着把任务发送给某个远程'AI 工厂'是完全可行的，工作在那个数据中心内部完成，最终结果再返回给用户……因为任务的经济价值远高于延迟敏感度（比如，一个自动化任务带来 500 美元的价值，但多花了一秒钟才返回），推理节点不需要在地理上贴近用户。"
—— @levie

这一论断的政策含义相当直接，正如 @adityaag 所指出的：

"如果建造数据中心变得更难，那么显然你应该大力押注那些已有现有算力的公司（也就是超大规模云厂商）。对新模型训练速度的影响会很明显。我猜我们确实会因此放慢前沿进展。民意如此。"
—— @adityaag

Replit CEO Amjad Masad 则从另一个角度印证了算力地缘政治的现实——他本周访问哈萨克斯坦，直言当地政府"超级 AI 信徒"，并认为这是 Network School 的理想落地地点。

📋 Claude Pro 定价层级厘清，以及那些不能错过的社区动态

Anthropic 员工 @thsottiaux 本周出来澄清了外界对 Claude Pro 计划的普遍误解：

"所有 Pro 计划均无五小时限制，使用量相比 Plus 如下：✅ Pro 100 = 10倍 ✅ Pro 200 = 20倍 ✅ Pro 500 = 50倍，并可访问超快速模式。"
—— @thsottiaux

他还发起了一个小调查——是否应该推出 Pro 50？——获得了超过 1300 个点赞，显示用户对更低价入门档有真实需求。

此外，风险投资人 @nikunj 发了一篇辛辣的讽刺贴，逐条解析创业公司如何在 Series A 融资时制造 FOMO——从"模糊晒收入曲线"到"永远没有 Deck 因为我们根本没在融资"。他最后补充道：

"（整篇是讽刺，但每一行单独拿出来都是真的。）"
—— @nikunj

而 Garry Tan 则以一贯的宏观叙事收尾本周："我们本可以拥有丰盛。这将是未来十年最核心的政治议题：我们能否通过超级智能实现科学、医学与工程的人类进步？还是我们会选择黑暗？"
